findings.title: View-only group permission allows top-level group creation
findings.body: canManage() accepts either the VIEW or MANAGE scope on all groups. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() calls requireManage(), which delegates to this method, so an administrator granted only read access can create groups or move an existing subgroup to the top level. Require MANAGE alone here and add a test that an all-groups VIEW permission cannot perform these mutations.

findings.title: Authorization resource IDs are used as group model IDs
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission() and returns it as a group ID. Authorization resources are created with generated IDs; the corresponding GroupModel ID is stored in the resource name by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(). Consequently the permission lookup misses the specific resource and falls back to all-groups permissions, and the returned IDs cannot match user group memberships when UsersResource applies the search filter. Use the mapped group model ID rather than the authorization resource ID, and handle the all-groups resource separately.

findings.title: Individual group resources are not assigned the Groups type
findings.body: When creating an individual group authorization resource, getOrCreateResource() sets its name and scopes but never sets its type to Groups. The new GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() discovers resources exclusively through findByType(..., "Groups", ...), so individual group permissions are omitted from that discovery. This prevents group-member permissions from supplying the group filters needed by user searches and counts. Assign the resource type when creating the resource and test discovery of an individual group's member-view permission.
